confidence_note: Written from memory and secondary knowledge of the book, no book text accessed. Seagate 3.5-inch prototype shown to customers who did not want it is recalled from the book's disk-drive chapters; exact dates, drive capacities, firm counts and Seagate's later outcome omitted. Old TR text quote ('successfully managed firms failed') is a paraphrase of the book's thesis, not a verified quotation. DB title is Turkish 'Yildirici Inovasyon'; English title assumed to be The Innovator's Dilemma from author and year.
facts: Christensen studied the disk drive industry across generations: 14-inch, 8-inch, 5.25-inch, 3.5-inch drives.
With each smaller size, leaders of the old size mostly did not lead the new one; newcomers did.
The failed leaders were well managed: they listened to best customers and invested in what those customers asked for.
Christensen argues those good management practices were the cause of their failure.
Smaller drives had less capacity, the measure mainframe and minicomputer customers cared about, so those customers did not want them.
New customers (desktop, later portable computer makers) valued small size and weight and accepted lower capacity.
Seagate's engineers built a 3.5-inch prototype and showed it to customers, who were not interested.
Small drives improved in capacity until they met the original customers' needs, and those customers moved.
scene_details: desktop and portable computer makers as the new buyers
tension: The best-run firms did everything customers asked and still lost the lead.
opening_idea: Seagate's engineers carry a small drive to customers who shrug.

lessons.idea: A product is judged by current users, who ask for more of the same, so the next buyers are easy to miss.
lessons.anchor: Seagate's customers shrugged at the 3.5-inch drive.

reflect_final: What do the people who never use your work today choose to use in its place?

use_cases.situation: Planning review, everyone wants features for current clients
use_cases.move: Ask who is not buying and what they use instead, pointing to Seagate's customers shrugging at the small drive.

use_cases.situation: Wanting backing for a skill current projects ignore
use_cases.move: Ask for a few hours a week to learn it.

use_cases.situation: Same few friends always give advice
use_cases.move: Ask one person outside the circle.

pocket_idea: Seagate's best customers shrugged at the small drive; ask someone outside your circle what they use.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: The leaders who lost weren't careless; they kept doing what best customers asked.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Seagate prototype shrug, then industry pattern, new buyers, drives improved.
